kolmogorov-zero-one-law.decisive_step: Tail event A independent of every finite prefix ⇒ independent of σ(X₁,X₂,…) ⊇ A ⇒ A independent of itself ⇒ P(A)=P(A)² ⇒ P(A)∈{0,1}

kolmogorov-zero-one-law.notes: Decisive step (extension-theorem uniqueness + self-independence) is Kolmogorov's own proof from the primary (Grundbegriffe/Foundations, treated here as primary); Norris/McNamara/Sheffield are only an alternate modern packaging (π-system route) and examples, deletable without breaking Route 1. anderson-localization.decisive_step: Track the probability distribution/typical value of the locator, not its ensemble average — mean diverges from rare resonances, giving the wrong (diffusive) answer.
anderson-localization.trace_passage: The trouble is that a real sample is not an ensemble, and a selected donor is not the average donor... The average is being set by events that almost never happen, so it answers the wrong question. I should track the probability distribution of the locator, or its typical value, not its mean.
anderson-localization.quote: What we really need to know is the probability distribution not its average... I would like to emphasize that this is the important, and deeply new, step taken here: the willingness to deal with distributions, not averages.
anderson-localization.notes: Nobel lecture already on disk explicitly frames distributions-vs-averages as the deep new step; reasoning.md mirrors this move/order closely (average->Portis diffusive answer trap, then typical-value fix).

bayesian-occam-factor.decisive_step: Recognizing P(D|H), the nuisance normalizer discarded in parameter fitting, as the model-comparison score; Laplace-approximating it gives best-fit likelihood x Occam factor (posterior/prior volume ratio)

bayesian-occam-factor.notes: Full Occam-factor/evidence/gamma derivation already in primary (mackay-1992) per source_matrix.md; explainers (ITILA ch28, azevedo-shachter, friel-wyse) used only for formula cross-check/navigation, not route-forcing; self_accounts/search_log.md explicitly says no discovery memoir found. material_on_disk true only because ITILA/explainer files exist (>2KB), not because they're load-bearing for the decisive step.

bellman-dynamic-programming.decisive_step: Tail of an optimal policy must itself be optimal for the state it reaches, collapsing the problem to a one-step max + continuation value.
bellman-dynamic-programming.trace_passage: If that tail is not optimal for the subproblem starting at the new state, then I could replace the tail with a better one... contradicting the assumed optimality of the whole policy.
bellman-dynamic-programming.notes: Self-account (Dreyfus/autobiography) present but source_matrix says it's kept out of the backbone (naming anecdote, incidental); Rust/Weber only verify modern theorem language, not replace primary. Decisive tail-swap argument is derivable from Bellman 1954 primary alone.

bcs-cooper-pairs.decisive_step: Restrict the variational superposition to paired configurations (k↑,-k↓ occupied together) so all off-diagonal matrix elements share one sign and reinforce, instead of the N-vs-N² wall killing the naive superposition.
bcs-cooper-pairs.trace_passage: I have N coefficients a_n but N^2 matrix elements to fix the signs of; I can't fix them all by choosing the a_n. So the naive superposition gains nothing. That's the wall.
bcs-cooper-pairs.quote: there are N2 matrix elements to be corrected with only N parameters a. We noticed that if the sum in (6) is restricted to include only configurations in which... its "mate" state is also occupied, then the matrix elements of H... would have a unique sign
bcs-cooper-pairs.notes: Already well-grounded via Schrieffer/Cooper/Bardeen Nobel lectures (self-accounts); grounding.md documents this explicitly. No fixer action needed; strong candidate as exemplar.

benign-overfitting.decisive_step: Isotropic case (Σ=I) shows raw dimension alone leaves tr(C)=Θ(1); benign behavior requires a wide, balanced low-variance tail (r_k, R_k conditions), not mere overparameterization.
benign-overfitting.trace_passage: Before trusting any of this, I should pin down whether overparameterization alone is enough... Take the most symmetric case: Sigma = I... This kills the simplest hypothesis: counting extra directions is not what makes interpolation benign.
benign-overfitting.notes: No self-account found (grounding.md documents exhaustive search, incl. mltheory.org 404). The decisive move (isotropic-case digression, r_k/R_k split) is the primary paper's own proof narrative, reproduced almost verbatim; ancestors give field context only, explainer (Bartlett-coauthored 2103.09177) is corroborating not forcing. refs/explainers/bartlett-montanari...2103.09177.txt (270KB) is the only >2KB non-primary self-adjacent material on disk, but it's a survey, not a discovery account; fixer would need to find an actual Bartlett talk/interview transcript if one exists.

bcs-theory.decisive_step: Restrict variational configurations to time-reversed pairs so pair-scattering matrix elements share one sign, enabling coherent energy lowering
bcs-theory.trace_passage: The way to keep a common sign is to restrict the important configurations so that states occur in time-reversed pairs: if `k up` is occupied, `-k down` is occupied.
bcs-theory.quote: if the sum in (6) is restricted to include only configurations in which, if any quasi-particle state...is occupied, its "mate" state is also occupied, then the matrix elements...would have a unique sign
bcs-theory.notes: Already well-grounded: Schrieffer Nobel lecture (self_accounts) documents exact obstacle (random sign cancellation) and resolution (paired-configuration restriction) mirrored in reasoning.md.

bandit-ucb-lai-robbins.decisive_step: Two-world change-of-measure argument (KL divergence between real and neighboring bandit) forcing E[T_i(n)] >= log n / KL(P_i,P_i*), the log n exploration lower bound
bandit-ucb-lai-robbins.trace_passage: The information-inequality route is cleaner and I prefer to lean on it. The KL divergence between the full histories under the two bandit worlds decomposes as D(P_nu || P_nu') = sum_j E_nu[T_j(n)] D(P_j || P_j')
bandit-ucb-lai-robbins.quote: Theorem 2.2 (Distribution-dependent lower bound)...We use the notation E,P when we integrate with respect to the modified bandit where the parameter of arm 2 is replaced by mu'_2. We want to compare the behavior of the forecaster on the initial and modified bandits
bandit-ucb-lai-robbins.notes: Genuine Lai-Robbins 1985 PDF unobtainable (documented, confirmed 403/HTML dead ends); decisive lower-bound proof is reconstructed entirely from Bubeck-Cesa-Bianchi survey Thm 2.2 + Lattimore-Szepesvari Thm 16.2, both third-party re-derivations explicitly citing L&R. berlekamp-massey.decisive_step: Repair uses a scaled+shifted copy of the last failing recurrence's residual (zero at all earlier-correct positions, -δ_f at its own fail point) to cancel new discrepancy δ_i minimally.
berlekamp-massey.trace_passage: Right now $C$ failed at $i$ with a known nonzero discrepancy... a previous recurrence — call it $B$... which was the current one up until the moment it failed at some position $f<i$
berlekamp-massey.notes: refs/ has OI-Wiki + CF-61306 (both used per notes/synthesis.md) but reasoning.md never cites them; decisive repair step is self-derived algebra, not traced to any source passage. banach-tarski-paradox.decisive_step: Free group F_2 on SO(3) rotations paradoxically decomposes itself; transport via orbit-choice set M gives paradoxical decomposition of S^2\D, absorb countable D by rotation shift.
banach-tarski-paradox.trace_passage: The group really does contain two disjoint copies of itself.
banach-tarski-paradox.notes: refs/ and src/ dirs don't exist; notes/sources.md only lists citations (Buchhorn arXiv, de la Harpe-Valette), no local source text/quotes. Reasoning is self-contained standard proof, not visibly forced by any non-primary passage.

barlow-twins.decisive_step: Redundancy-reduction loss (cross-correlation → I) makes non-collapse the optimum by construction, replacing negatives/predictor/stop-grad/clustering

berry-phase.decisive_step: Refuse to assume the loop phase is exhausted by the dynamical phase; carry an undetermined extra γ_n through Schrödinger's eq, motivated by Fox's magnetic-field/sign-change question.
berry-phase.trace_passage: And then Fox asks the innocent thing: put a magnetic field in the billiard, charge the particle, break time-reversal symmetry... So what happens to the sign change as I continue the wavefunction around the very same loop that used to surround the coincidence?
berry-phase.quote: At the end of the lecture, the Chairman of the physics department, Professor Ron Fox, asked the innocent question: "When a degeneracy is destroyed by a magnetic field, what happens to the sign change...round the circuit"
berry-phase.notes: Already well-grounded (notes/synthesis.md cites berry1990_anticipations.pdf explicitly as genesis source); little for a fixer to do besides verify quotes match.

bernnet.decisive_step: Non-negative Bernstein basis is the (unique-family) basis where nonneg coeffs<=>nonneg polynomial, solving the g(lambda)>=0 validity constraint that monomial/Chebyshev bases fail.
bernnet.trace_passage: The classical result rescues it via degree elevation...Powers and Reznick make the degree requirement explicit.

bc.decisive_step: Image-transform trick: resample sensor image to synthesize off-center/rotated views + pure-pursuit label correction, fixing no-recovery-examples and overlearning-recent-input walls

bayesian-rl-psrl.decisive_step: Posterior symmetry E[g(M*)|H]=E[g(M_k)|H] removes the unobservable true-optimal comparator, replacing it with the sampled policy's own executed value.

bayesian-rl-psrl.notes: Trace is a self-contained rederivation (identity, simulation lemma, telescoping, UCRL2 confidence widths) that matches primary paper content exactly; no citation/quote of any non-primary source appears despite rich self_accounts/explainers on disk (e.g. Osband&VanRoy 2016 'why PS beats optimism').

binary-sign.decisive_step: l2-optimal binarization: minimize ||W-αB||² forces B*=sign(W), α*=mean|W| (from XNOR-Net, a primary paper)
binary-sign.trace_passage: minimizing `J` over `B` is exactly *maximizing* `WᵀB = Σ_i W_i B_i` subject to `B_i ∈ {−1,+1}`

black-scholes.decisive_step: Write w(x,t) via Treynor's value-equation approach, keep the second-derivative term, apply CAPM to cancel drift α, then choose zero-beta drift so both discounting holes close
black-scholes.trace_passage: Treynor taught me this when I was at Arthur D. Little — he had a "value equation," ... I remember his equation had an error: he had dropped some second-derivative terms, and it didn't come right until we put them back.
black-scholes.quote: His equation had an error because he had omitted some terms involving second derivatives, but we found out how to put in the missing terms and correct the equation.
black-scholes.notes: refs/src already hold Black 1989 self-account, Scholes/Merton Nobel lectures, Merton 1973 — well-covered; no further web hunt needed

beta-calibration.decisive_step: Replace sigmoid's equal-variance Gaussian per-class score model with beta distributions, deriving LR(s)=e^c s^a/(1-s)^b, which is fittable as bivariate logistic regression on (ln s, -ln(1-s))
beta-calibration.trace_passage: Where did the trouble enter? The Gaussian: infinite support, and a single shared variance that pins the slope and forbids the gathering shape. My score lives on `[0, 1]`. What's the natural density on `[0, 1]`? The beta distribution.
beta-calibration.notes: reasoning.md is a self-contained rederivation of Kull et al. 2017's own Propositions 1-2; no netcal/sklearn/author-page/Platt/Niculescu source is cited or named in the trace itself, though self_accounts (betacal_author_page.html) and explainers exist unused on disk (>2KB) if a fixer wants to route through them.

bell-inequality.decisive_step: Reject von Neumann's additivity axiom on dispersion-free states as unjustified (Stern-Gerlach orientation argument), reopening hidden variables and motivating locality as the real constraint.
bell-inequality.trace_passage: The expectation value of σ_x for a magnetic particle is measured with a Stern–Gerlach magnet pointing along x...σ_x + σ_y...is measured with the magnet along a *third*, diagonal orientation. These are three different experiments.
bell-inequality.quote: the measurement of for a magnetic particle might be made with a suitably oriented Stern Gerlach magnet. The measurement of o-would require a different orientation, and...a third and different orientation.
bell-inequality.notes: bell1966_hiddenvars.txt is Bell's own companion paper (self-account, distinct from primary bell1964 EPR paper); its Sec II-III additivity/Stern-Gerlach argument is the source for the von Neumann critique opening the reasoning.

blum-speedup.decisive_step: Speedup must be non-uniform (diagonalization against Phi_i, priority/cancellation over indices) since an effective optimizer would let a program beat itself.
blum-speedup.trace_passage: So the speedup, if it exists, has to be non-uniform: the faster program exists but is not handed to me by an effective procedure applied to the slower one.
blum-speedup.notes: No refs/ or src/ dirs exist; notes/sources.md lists only the primary Blum 1967 paper plus two secondary sites (MathWorld, Wikipedia) explicitly used only as paraphrase checks, not grounding. Reasoning is a self-contained re-derivation. Fixer needs a full web hunt for a genuine self-account (e.g. van Emde Boas survey, Blum's thesis).

blum-micali-prg.decisive_step: Reverse output order (emit B(f^m(x)),...,B(f(x))) so predicting next bit requires computing B at points the generator itself never computes.
blum-micali-prg.trace_passage: If I emit bits in forward order I have the asymmetry backwards ... I compute an orbit and arrange the output from the far end back toward the seed
blum-micali-prg.notes: Decisive step (reversed-order emission, hard predicate B) is developed straight from the primary FOCS/SIAM paper; Ben Lynn explainer files exist (>2KB) but are never named/relied on in reasoning.md, so this reads as single-source.

bait.decisive_step: Derive Bayes risk = σ²tr(Λ⁻¹Σ), forcing A-optimal weighted-trace objective over D-optimal determinant
bait.trace_passage: Two completely different derivations — Bayesian risk and frequentist MLE error — land on `tr((Σ_{x∈S} I(x;θ))^{-1} I_U(θ))`. When two independent routes converge on the same functional, that's the object to trust.
bait.notes: Chaudhuri ancestor + official bait_sampling.py/strategy.py code already on disk (>2KB) but used only to corroborate/confirm formulas already derivable from primary's own Bayes-risk derivation; no author self-account found (search_log.md documents absence).

biggan.decisive_step: Diagnosing instability as a D-G interaction (memorization/zero-gradient drift) not fixable by G-conditioning alone; truncation trick needs G smoothness -> off-diagonal orthogonal reg
biggan.trace_passage: Stability isn't a property of G's conditioning, and it isn't a property of D's conditioning; it's a property of their *interaction* through the adversarial game.

One code line (`2*mm(mm(w,w.t())*(1-eye),w)`) attributed to BigGAN-PyTorch is quoted but the repo isn't on disk and it's used only to sanity-check a gradient factor, not to force the decisive design step; fixer would need to web-hunt Brock's blog/interviews or ICLR OpenReview for a genuine non-primary account.

block-topk.decisive_step: Score blocks via mean-pooled q · mean-pooled k (linear = exact block aggregate), force-include diagonal block, solve density budget for K via quadratic.
block-topk.trace_passage: So the mean key is not an approximation of the block's aggregate logit at all — up to the constant factor `Bk` it *is* the aggregate, exactly.
block-topk.notes: refs/notes cite lucidrains impl + Medium explainers only in notes files (framing/structure), never woven into reasoning.md as a dependency; decisive step derived from primary NSA/Quest/InfLLM/MInference papers only.

brouwer-fixed-point.decisive_step: Replacing Brouwer's own degree-theoretic proof with the Sperner-lemma combinatorial route (rooms/doors parity argument + gradient coloring) as the theorem's spine.
brouwer-fixed-point.trace_passage: Think of each little triangle as a room and each door as a doorway between rooms (or to the outside). Count the doors *per room*.
brouwer-fixed-point.quote: A room with exactly 1 door is called a dead end, while a room with exactly 2 doors is called a communicating room. A door may either lead to another room...or it may lead outside

Already well-sourced; little for fixer to add.

byol.notes: No refs/ dir exists; src/ is only the primary BYOL paper's own tex sources (ablation/appendix/method), no author blog/OpenReview/third-party material present on disk.

chebnet.decisive_step: Restrict spectral filter g_θ(Λ) to a degree-(K-1) polynomial of L, then realize it via Chebyshev 3-term recurrence for O(K|E|) eigendecomposition-free filtering

No non-primary source cited anywhere in reasoning.md (checked for Bruna, Hammond/Vandergheynst/Gribonval discussion, blogs, code, OpenReview) — pure primary-paper rewrite; fixer needs a web hunt for author account/code if upgrading.

cap-set.decisive_step: Generalize CLP's 2-var polynomial-rank lemma to symmetric α=β=γ=1 in F_3, then balance degree threshold d=2(q-1)n/3 to get exponential saving.

bpp-in-sigma2.decisive_step: View accepting strings as subset A_x of {0,1}^m under XOR; a small list of random shifts covers the cube iff A_x is dense, cannot cover it iff A_x is sparse (Sigma_2 witness).
bpp-in-sigma2.trace_passage: What made this work was refusing to look for good random strings and instead reading the accepting set as a subset of a group, where density and sparsity become the presence or absence of a small covering by translates.

photonic-inverse-design.trace_passage: Now the move. The Maxwell Green's function is reciprocal: G^EP(x₀, x) = G^EP(x, x₀)^T. A dipole at x seen at x₀ equals a dipole at x₀ seen at x, with the tensor transposed.

pcp-theorem.decisive_step: Compose outer algebraic verifier with an inner verifier checking its tiny decision circuit, shrinking answer size to O(1) bits while keeping O(log n) randomness.
pcp-theorem.trace_passage: This is composition. The outer verifier supplies low randomness and algebraic robustness. The inner verifier checks the tiny decision problem created by the outer verifier's random choice.

ppo-lag.decisive_step: Fix PPO's exploding step-size as λ grows by rescaling combined advantage A=(A_r−λA_c)/(1+λ) instead of raw A_r−λA_c.

prime-number-theorem.decisive_step: Zeta has no zeros on Re(s)=1, via positivity from 3+4cos u+cos 2u≥0 applied to log|ζ(σ)^3ζ(σ+it)^4ζ(σ+2it)|

q-learning-watkins.quote: if the values of Q differ from the optimal values Q*, then the implicit policy may differ from the optimal policy... a small perturbation of Q away from the optimum may under some circumstances lead to instability
q-learning-watkins.notes: Thesis (self-account relative to compressed 1992 paper) p97-98 admission is the sole ground for restricting to one-step; also self_accounts/watkins-rl-some-history.html present, unused for this step.

platt-scaling.decisive_step: Numerically-stable NLL reformulation (branch on sign of Af+B to avoid overflow/log(0)/cancellation) + Hessian-is-Gram-matrix convexity proof that licenses damped Newton

But the sign-branch stable NLL trick and Gram-matrix/Cauchy-Schwarz convexity proof (Theorem 1) that reasoning.md reproduces near-verbatim are Lin-Lin-Weng's own fix to Platt's crude 'log(0)=-200' hack — primary alone can't justify them. shor-algorithm.decisive_step: Route decisive step: generalize Simon's binary Fourier period-finding to discrete log FIRST (via smooth-number special case) before generalizing to factoring, rather than deriving factoring directly
shor-algorithm.quote: Looking back to Simon's work, the transformation that he used was a Fourier transform and that made me think how Fourier transformations could be applied ... to solve the discrete logarithmic problem.
shor-algorithm.trace_passage: Discrete logarithm jumps out first. Fix a prime `p` and a generator `g` of the cyclic group mod `p`... Simon's Hadamard won't do. I need the honest Fourier transform over a *cyclic* group
shor-algorithm.notes: Already well-grounded via compiled self-account (CERN interview + Physics Today quotes); discovery order (Simon->discrete log->smooth case->generalize to factoring) matches interviews exactly. No fixer action needed.

sensitivity-conjecture-cube.decisive_step: Sign Q^n's edges so pseudo-adjacency A_n^2=nI, forcing eigenvalues ±√n split evenly; Cauchy interlacing then gives every (2^{n-1}+1)-vertex induced subgraph Δ(H)≥λ1≥√n.

submodular-greedy.decisive_step: Averaging greedy's gain over OPT's elements, then using submodularity to dominate the joint gain f(S_i∪O), then monotonicity to reach f(OPT); yields the (1-1/k) contraction giving (1-1/e).

ste.decisive_step: Backward pass replaces the hard threshold's a.e.-zero Jacobian with the identity (not the sigmoid-derivative), since identity keeps signal alive in saturation.
ste.trace_passage: the identity proxy assigns slope +1... So the cruder proxy is the better one here, and the reason is concrete: it refuses to attenuate where I need signal most.
ste.notes: Primary (arxiv-dcc1.tex l.680-690) itself states identity-vs-sigmoid-derivative choice and 'right sign, single layer' near-verbatim; reasoning.md's descent-direction proof (paras 47-49) is self-derived, echoing Yin et al. 1903.05662's theorem but that paper is not on disk (only cited in notes/explainer.md); hinton_lec15.pdf on disk is the wrong lecture content (flagged in notes, not actually usable). REINFORCE/SPSA papers used only to explore/reject alternatives, not to force the decisive step. No non-primary material is load-bearing for the final choice itself.

stochastic-depth.decisive_step: Per-minibatch Bernoulli gate zeroing f_ℓ (exact identity via non-negative ReLU shortcut) + linear survival decay + test-time p_ℓ-rescaling of f_ℓ
stochastic-depth.trace_passage: Make that concrete. For each block introduce a Bernoulli gate b_ℓ ∈ {0,1}, drawn fresh each mini-batch, and multiply the transformation by it
stochastic-depth.notes: refs has self_accounts/github_readme.md and explainers/aleju_stochastic_depth.md (>2KB) but unused; entire decisive step (gate, ReLU-identity check, linear decay, test rescaling) rederived straight from primary paper + authors' own ResidualDrop.lua/main.lua code, no non-primary dependency in the trace.

structural-risk-minimization.trace_passage: I therefore organize the search into a structure `S1 subset S2 subset ... subset Sn`... The final choice is not the candidate with the lowest training error. It is the candidate with the lowest guaranteed risk bound
structural-risk-minimization.notes: reasoning.md is a clean rewrite of Vapnik 1991/1999 primaries; no self-account/explainer terms (Chervonenkis, Gammerman/Vovk, 'venereal-clinic') appear anywhere in the trace despite notes/ claiming self-account was 'used'.

tarski-fixed-point.decisive_step: Define P={x|f(x)<=x}, take a=meet P, show f(a)<=a and a<=f(a) via monotonicity to get least fixed point a=f(a)
tarski-fixed-point.trace_passage: Define `P = {x in L | f(x) <= x}`... `a = meet P`... `f(a) <= a` and `a <= f(a)`. So `f(a) = a`.

symmetric-ce.decisive_step: Symmetrize KL(q||p) into KL(q||p)+KL(p||q), giving RCE=-Σp_k log q_k; define log0:=A to make RCE finite and class-sum constant, hence noise-tolerant.
symmetric-ce.trace_passage: "So why am I only measuring discrepancy in the direction that trusts q? Measure it the other way too: KL(p||q)... Symmetrize: SKL = KL(q||p) + KL(p||q)."

timesnet.trace_passage: Reshape the 1D series, for a discovered period p, into a 2D tensor whose two axes are exactly intraperiod and interperiod, and the two variations I care about both become local in 2D.

ternary-158bit.decisive_step: Two-stage LR (high peak, decay midway) and two-stage weight-decay (0.1 then off) schedule, justified by S-shaped loss curve and latent-weight-as-confidence-score argument

turan-symmetrization.decisive_step: Two-case vertex-duplication (clone higher-degree endpoint; if u is local max, clone u twice) proving edge-maximal K_{r+1}-free graph is complete multipartite

turan-symmetrization.quote: If d(y1) > d(x), then deleting x and duplicating y1 yields another K r-free graph with more edges than G ... deleting both y1 and y2 and duplicating x twice yields a K r-free graph with more edges
turan-symmetrization.notes: Duplication trick is Diestel's/Aigner-Ziegler's "second/fifth proof" (Zykov), not Turán's own 1941 induction proof; primary alone can't yield this route. Attribute explicitly.
